chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Fadhal from Muawiyah ibn Wahb from Abi Salam from Sawrah ibn Kulayb from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: What is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And on the Day of Judgment you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'One who claims to be an Imam while he is not an Imam.' I said: 'Even if he is Alawi and Fatimi?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, even if he is Alawi and Fatimi.'
ai.seo_question: Who does the verse 'their faces blackened' refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the divine punishment for 'blackened faces' applies to any self-proclaimed Imam who lacks true authority, explicitly noting that even a claimant from the prestigious lineage of Ali and Fatima is not exempt. This underscores the Shia principle that Imamate is a divine appointment requiring specific qualifications, rather than a hereditary right automatically conferred by bloodline alone. The narration serves as a critical criterion for distinguishing true Imams from pretenders during periods of occultation or succession disputes.
